description: Regional Accessibility of Post-Earthquake Emergency Healthcare in Metro Vancouver, BC is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Kiran Kaur, University of British Columbia (ubc.ca). The system under investigation is the regional network of emergency healthcare facilities and transportation infrastructure in Metro Vancouver, British Columbia. This dataset was developed to support a regional assessment of healthcare accessibility following a major earthquake hazard, specifically under a suite of physics-based Cascadia Subduction Zone (CSZ) M9 earthquake scenarios. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project with 11 top-level files (DOCX, XLSX, CSV, LYRX). Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-2th1-6q44. Keywords: Post-earthquake emergency healthcare accessibility,  hospital network,  transportation network,  interdependent infrastructure, enhanced two-step floating catchment area analysis, Cascadia Subduction Zone. Published 2025-11-14. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
